HE-1.t: Identify erythrocytes, neutrophils, bands, eosinophils, basophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, and platelets on a Wright-stained peripheral smear by cell size, nuclear shape, and granule color.
Trace hematopoiesis from the hematopoietic stem cell through common myeloid and common lymphoid progenitors to each mature blood cell lineage.

Describe the sequence of hematopoietic sites in development (yolk sac, then liver and spleen, then bone marrow) and relate marrow fibrosis and ineffective erythropoiesis (beta thalassemia major) after birth to extramedullary hematopoiesis and splenomegaly.

Describe erythroid maturation from proerythroblast through reticulocyte to mature erythrocyte, including nuclear condensation and extrusion, hemoglobin accumulation, and loss of residual ribosomal RNA, and explain what an elevated reticulocyte count indicates about marrow response.
HE-1.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia

HE-1.t: Describe granulocyte maturation from myeloblast through promyelocyte, myelocyte, metamyelocyte, and band to segmented neutrophil, and identify a left shift on a peripheral smear.

Describe platelet formation by fragmentation of megakaryocyte cytoplasm and identify platelet granule contents: alpha granules (von Willebrand factor, fibrinogen) and dense granules (ADP, calcium, serotonin).

Locate B cell and T cell zones in the lymph node (cortical follicles, paracortex, medullary cords and sinuses) and the spleen (white pulp, periarteriolar lymphoid sheath, marginal zone, red pulp cords and sinusoids).

HE-2.t: Describe the composition of plasma (water, albumin, globulins, fibrinogen, electrolytes) and distinguish plasma from serum.
Explain the roles of albumin in plasma oncotic pressure and in transport of bilirubin, fatty acids, and calcium, and predict edema from hypoalbuminemia using Starling forces.

Describe red cell features that support gas transport (biconcave shape, no nucleus or mitochondria, carbonic anhydrase converting CO2 to bicarbonate, chloride shift) and explain their functional advantages.
Explain how erythropoietin from renal peritubular interstitial cells responds to tissue hypoxia, and predict erythropoietin levels in chronic kidney disease, high altitude, and polycythemia vera.
HE-2.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: polycythemia

HE-2.t: Interpret a complete blood count with hemoglobin, hematocrit, MCV, MCHC, RDW, and reticulocyte count to classify an anemia as microcytic, normocytic, or macrocytic and as underproduction or hemolytic.
HE-2.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia

HE-2.t: Explain the functions of neutrophils, eosinophils, basophils, monocytes, and lymphocytes, and relate neutrophilia, eosinophilia, and lymphocytosis to bacterial infection, parasitic or allergic disease, and viral infection.
HE-2.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: leukocytosis

HE-2.t: Describe ABO and Rh antigens and naturally occurring IgM anti-A and anti-B antibodies, and predict compatible donors for red cell and plasma transfusion.
HE-2.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Reactions to blood components: ABO incompatibility

HE-3.t: Describe the red cell life span of about 120 days and the removal of senescent red cells by macrophages of the spleen and liver.

Trace heme catabolism from heme to biliverdin (heme oxygenase) and unconjugated bilirubin (biliverdin reductase), albumin transport, hepatic conjugation by UDP-glucuronosyltransferase, and excretion as urobilinogen, urobilin, and stercobilin.
HE-3.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: hemolysis

HE-3.t: Distinguish intravascular from extravascular hemolysis using haptoglobin, LDH, unconjugated bilirubin, hemoglobinuria, hemosiderinuria, and smear findings (schistocytes versus spherocytes).
HE-3.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: hemolysis

HE-3.t: Explain iron recycling and absorption: duodenal uptake of ferrous iron by DMT1, export through ferroportin, transferrin transport, ferritin storage, and hepcidin inhibition of ferroportin.
HE-3.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Nutrition: mineral deficiencies and/or toxicities

HE-3.t: Relate the short circulating life of neutrophils (hours) and platelets (about 7 to 10 days) compared with red cells to explain why neutropenia and thrombocytopenia appear before anemia after sudden marrow suppression.
HE-3.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: pancytopenia

HE-4.t: Identify the growth factors that drive each lineage: erythropoietin for red cells, G-CSF and GM-CSF for granulocytes, thrombopoietin for megakaryocytes, and IL-5 for eosinophils.

Describe primary hemostasis: vasoconstriction, von Willebrand factor bridging exposed collagen to platelet GpIb, platelet degranulation with ADP and thromboxane A2 release, and fibrinogen linking GpIIb/IIIa receptors during aggregation.

Trace secondary hemostasis through the tissue factor (extrinsic) and contact (intrinsic) pathways to the common pathway, thrombin generation, and fibrin cross-linking by factor XIIIa, and relate PT and PTT to each pathway.

Explain how antithrombin, thrombomodulin with proteins C and S, and tissue factor pathway inhibitor limit clotting, and how plasmin from tPA-activated plasminogen produces fibrin degradation products and D-dimer.
HE-4.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Coagulation disorders: hypercoagulable

HE-4.t: Interpret platelet count, bleeding time, PT/INR, PTT, fibrinogen, and a mixing study to localize a bleeding disorder to platelets, a specific coagulation pathway, a factor inhibitor, or consumption.
HE-4.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Coagulation disorders: hypocoagulable

HE-4.t: Describe Virchow triad (stasis, endothelial injury, hypercoagulability) and relate immobility, surgery, pregnancy, malignancy, and estrogen use to venous thrombosis risk.
HE-4.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Coagulation disorders: hypercoagulable

HE-5.t: Trace heme synthesis from glycine and succinyl-CoA through ALA synthase (rate limiting, pyridoxine dependent), ALA dehydratase, and ferrochelatase, locating mitochondrial and cytosolic steps and explaining heme feedback on ALA synthase.
HE-5.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Genetic, metabolic, and developmental disorders: porphyria

HE-5.t: Distinguish acute intermittent porphyria (porphobilinogen deaminase deficiency, abdominal pain, neuropsychiatric symptoms, high urine porphobilinogen) from porphyria cutanea tarda (uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase deficiency, blistering photosensitivity, hepatitis C association).
HE-5.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Genetic, metabolic, and developmental disorders: porphyria

HE-5.t: Describe the globin chains of hemoglobin A, A2, and F, explain cooperative oxygen binding, and predict shifts of the oxygen dissociation curve with 2,3-BPG, H+, CO2, temperature, fetal hemoglobin, and carbon monoxide.
HE-5.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: disorders of hemoglobin

HE-5.t: Explain how ferric iron in methemoglobin and carbon monoxide binding reduce oxygen delivery despite a normal PaO2, and identify congenital (cytochrome b5 reductase deficiency) and acquired (nitrites, dapsone, benzocaine) methemoglobinemia.
HE-5.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: congenital methemoglobinemia

HE-5.t: Explain why red cells depend on glycolysis and the pentose phosphate pathway, and relate pyruvate kinase deficiency to ATP loss and G6PD deficiency to NADPH and reduced glutathione loss with oxidative hemolysis.
HE-5.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: hemolysis

HE-5.t: Explain the roles of vitamin B12 and folate in thymidine synthesis, methionine synthase, and methylmalonyl-CoA mutase, and use methylmalonic acid and homocysteine levels to distinguish B12 from folate deficiency.
HE-5.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Nutrition: vitamin deficiencies and/or toxicities: vitamin B12, vitamin B9

HE-5.t: Explain vitamin K dependent gamma-carboxylation of factors II, VII, IX, and X and proteins C and S, and why these carboxylated residues need calcium to bind phosphatidylserine on activated platelet membranes.
HE-5.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Nutrition: vitamin deficiencies and/or toxicities: vitamin K

HE-6.t: Explain how a glutamate to valine substitution at position 6 of beta globin causes HbS polymerization when deoxygenated, and predict how fetal hemoglobin, dehydration, acidosis, and hypoxia change sickling.
HE-6.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: sickle cell disease

HE-6.t: Relate the number of deleted alpha globin genes (one to four) to silent carrier, alpha thalassemia trait, HbH disease, and Hb Barts hydrops fetalis, and contrast beta thalassemia caused by point mutations (often splice site or promoter).
HE-6.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: thalassemias

HE-6.t: Identify the inheritance of hemophilia A and B and G6PD deficiency (X-linked recessive), sickle cell disease and thalassemias (autosomal recessive), and most hereditary spherocytosis and von Willebrand disease (autosomal dominant), and predict offspring risk.
HE-6.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia

HE-6.t: Explain how t(9;22) forms the BCR-ABL1 fusion gene with constitutive tyrosine kinase activity in CML, and how the JAK2 V617F mutation drives growth factor independent proliferation in polycythemia vera.

Relate characteristic translocations to the genes they deregulate: t(8;14) MYC in Burkitt lymphoma, t(14;18) BCL2 (blocked apoptosis) in follicular lymphoma, t(11;14) cyclin D1 in mantle cell lymphoma, and t(15;17) PML-RARA (blocked differentiation) in acute promyelocytic leukemia.
Explain how defective DNA crosslink repair in Fanconi anemia causes congenital marrow failure with short stature, thumb and radial anomalies, and increased risk of AML.
HE-6.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Neoplasms: inherited cancer syndromes: DNA repair abnormalities (Fanconi anemia)

HE-6.t: Explain how factor V Leiden (resistance to activated protein C) and the prothrombin G20210A mutation (increased prothrombin levels) raise venous thrombosis risk.
HE-6.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Coagulation disorders: hypercoagulable: factor V Leiden, prothrombin G20210A mutation

HE-7.t: Distinguish warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia (IgG, extravascular, spherocytes; SLE, CLL) from cold agglutinin disease (IgM with complement; Mycoplasma pneumoniae, EBV), and interpret a positive direct Coombs test.
HE-7.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Infectious and immunologic: autoimmune hemolytic anemia

HE-7.t: Classify hematologic immune reactions by hypersensitivity type: acute hemolytic transfusion reaction, autoimmune hemolysis, and hemolytic disease of the newborn (type II), and cryoglobulinemia with immune complex vasculitis (type III).
HE-7.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Infectious and immunologic: cryoglobulinemia

HE-7.t: Distinguish acute hemolytic, delayed hemolytic, febrile nonhemolytic, and anaphylactic (IgA deficiency) transfusion reactions, septic reactions from contaminated units, and TRALI by mechanism, timing, and key findings.
HE-7.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Reactions to blood components

HE-7.t: Explain how IgG antibodies against heparin and platelet factor 4 complexes activate platelets in heparin-induced thrombocytopenia, producing a falling platelet count with arterial and venous thrombosis.
HE-7.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Coagulation disorders: hypercoagulable: heparin-induced thrombocytopenia

HE-7.t: Explain how antiphospholipid antibodies (lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, anti-beta2 glycoprotein I) cause arterial and venous thrombosis and pregnancy loss despite prolonging the PTT in vitro.
HE-7.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Coagulation disorders: hypercoagulable: anticardiolipin antibodies, lupus anticoagulant

HE-7.t: Explain how Epstein-Barr virus enters B cells through CD21, produces atypical CD8 T cell lymphocytosis in mononucleosis, and contributes to Burkitt lymphoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, and lymphomas in immunosuppressed patients.

Explain why asplenia (surgical or sickle cell autosplenectomy) raises risk of sepsis from encapsulated organisms (Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae type b, Neisseria meningitidis) and why vaccination against them is protective.
HE-7.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Traumatic, mechanical, and vascular disorders: splenectomy effects/complications

HE-8.t: Trace the Plasmodium life cycle from sporozoite inoculation by the female Anopheles mosquito through liver schizogony, the erythrocytic cycle, and gametocytes, and explain relapse from hypnozoites of P. vivax and P. ovale.
HE-8.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Infectious and immunologic: malaria

HE-8.t: Explain the virulence of Plasmodium falciparum: invasion of red cells of all ages, high parasitemia, PfEMP1-mediated adherence of infected red cells to endothelium causing microvascular obstruction, and immune evasion by switching var genes that encode PfEMP1.
HE-8.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Infectious and immunologic: malaria

HE-8.t: Explain how sickle cell trait, G6PD deficiency, and thalassemia trait reduce severe malaria, and why Duffy antigen negative red cells resist Plasmodium vivax invasion.
HE-8.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Infectious and immunologic: malaria

HE-8.t: Describe Babesia microti transmission by Ixodes scapularis ticks and by transfusion, its intraerythrocytic ring forms and Maltese cross tetrads, and coinfection with Borrelia burgdorferi.
HE-8.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Infectious and immunologic: babesiosis

HE-8.t: Describe the Schistosoma life cycle: freshwater snail intermediate host, cercarial skin penetration, adult worms in mesenteric (S. mansoni, S. japonicum) or vesical (S. haematobium) venules, and egg deposition.

Explain how parvovirus B19, a nonenveloped single-stranded DNA virus, infects erythroid progenitors through the P antigen, causing transient aplastic crisis in chronic hemolytic anemias and hydrops fetalis in fetal infection.
HE-8.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Infectious and immunologic: viral

HE-9-A.t: Identify causes of iron deficiency anemia (chronic gastrointestinal or menstrual blood loss, poor intake or absorption, pregnancy) and predict its profile: low ferritin, high TIBC, low transferrin saturation, high RDW, and microcytic hypochromic cells.
HE-9-A.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: decreased production

HE-9-A.t: Distinguish iron deficiency, anemia of chronic disease (IL-6 driven hepcidin, high ferritin, low TIBC), thalassemia trait (normal iron studies, target cells), and sideroblastic anemia (high iron, ringed sideroblasts) using iron studies and smear.
HE-9-A.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: anemia of chronic disease

HE-9-A.t: Explain how lead inhibition of ALA dehydratase and ferrochelatase, alcohol, pyridoxine deficiency, and X-linked ALAS2 mutations cause sideroblastic anemia, and identify basophilic stippling and high zinc protoporphyrin in lead poisoning.
HE-9-A.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: sideroblastic anemia

HE-9-A.t: Explain how pernicious anemia (antibodies to parietal cells and intrinsic factor), ileal resection, and the fish tapeworm Dibothriocephalus (formerly Diphyllobothrium) latus cause B12 deficiency with megaloblastic anemia, hypersegmented neutrophils, and subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord.
HE-9-A.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Nutrition: vitamin deficiencies and/or toxicities: vitamin B12 (pernicious anemia)

HE-9-A.t: Identify causes of folate deficiency (poor intake, alcohol use, pregnancy, chronic hemolysis, methotrexate) and distinguish megaloblastic anemia from nonmegaloblastic macrocytosis due to liver disease, alcohol, and reticulocytosis.
HE-9-A.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Nutrition: vitamin deficiencies and/or toxicities: vitamin B9

HE-9-A.t: Explain aplastic anemia as stem cell failure from autoimmune T cell injury, drugs, benzene, radiation, viral hepatitis, or Fanconi anemia, and identify pancytopenia with a hypocellular fatty marrow and no splenomegaly.
HE-9-A.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: aplastic anemia

HE-9-A.t: Distinguish polycythemia vera (JAK2 V617F, low erythropoietin, aquagenic pruritus, splenomegaly) from secondary polycythemia with appropriately high erythropoietin (hypoxia, altitude, smoking) or inappropriately high erythropoietin (renal cell or hepatocellular carcinoma), and from relative polycythemia.
HE-9-A.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: polycythemia vera, secondary polycythemia

HE-9-A.t: Predict complications of polycythemia vera from hyperviscosity and thrombosis (stroke, Budd-Chiari syndrome, erythromelalgia), high cell turnover (gout), and progression to myelofibrosis or acute myeloid leukemia.
HE-9-A.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: polycythemia vera

HE-9-A.t: Predict hemoglobin, reticulocyte, and iron changes after acute blood loss (normal hemoglobin at first, fall after fluid shift, reticulocytosis in days) and after chronic blood loss (iron deficiency).
HE-9-A.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: blood loss anemia

HE-9-A.t: Classify neutropenia by mechanism (marrow failure, drug-induced agranulocytosis such as with propylthiouracil, immune destruction, cyclic neutropenia from ELANE mutation) and relate an absolute neutrophil count below 500/µL to severe bacterial and fungal infection risk.
HE-9-A.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: neutropenia, agranulocytosis

HE-9-A.t: Distinguish a leukemoid reaction (neutrophilia with left shift, toxic granulation, high leukocyte alkaline phosphatase) from chronic myeloid leukemia (basophilia, low leukocyte alkaline phosphatase, BCR-ABL1).
HE-9-A.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: leukocytosis

HE-9-B.t: Predict complications of sickle cell disease from vaso-occlusion and hemolysis: dactylitis, acute chest syndrome, stroke, splenic autoinfarction, Salmonella osteomyelitis, renal papillary necrosis, priapism, pigment gallstones, and aplastic crisis.
HE-9-B.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: sickle cell disease

HE-9-B.t: Explain how beta thalassemia major causes ineffective erythropoiesis, extramedullary hematopoiesis (crew-cut skull, maxillary overgrowth), hepatosplenomegaly, and iron overload, and interpret electrophoresis showing high HbA2 in beta thalassemia minor.
HE-9-B.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: thalassemias

HE-9-B.t: Explain how G6PD deficiency causes episodic intravascular hemolysis after oxidant stress (infection, fava beans, sulfonamides, primaquine, dapsone), and identify Heinz bodies and bite cells on smear.
HE-9-B.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: G6PD deficiency

HE-9-B.t: Explain how ankyrin, spectrin, or band 3 defects in hereditary spherocytosis cause membrane loss and splenic trapping, and predict spherocytes, high MCHC, splenomegaly, pigment gallstones, abnormal osmotic fragility or EMA binding, and a negative Coombs test.
HE-9-B.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: hereditary spherocytosis

HE-9-B.t: Explain how maternal anti-D IgG formed after prior Rh-positive fetal exposure crosses the placenta to cause fetal hemolysis, anemia, and hydrops fetalis, and contrast milder ABO hemolytic disease in infants of group O mothers.
HE-9-B.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Reactions to blood components: Rh incompatibility

HE-9-B.t: Interpret a positive direct Coombs test in the newborn and indirect Coombs test in the mother, and predict rising unconjugated bilirubin and kernicterus risk after birth when placental clearance ends.
HE-9-B.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Reactions to blood components: Rh incompatibility

HE-9-B.t: Explain how an acquired PIGA mutation in paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria removes GPI-anchored CD55 and CD59, causing complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis, venous thrombosis, and cytopenias detected by flow cytometry.
HE-9-B.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Infectious and immunologic: paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria

HE-9-B.t: Describe pyruvate kinase deficiency (autosomal recessive, ATP depletion, rigid red cells, extravascular hemolysis) and hereditary elliptocytosis (spectrin defects, elliptocytes, usually mild hemolysis).
HE-9-B.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: pyruvate kinase deficiency, hereditary elliptocytosis

HE-9-B.t: Distinguish thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (ADAMTS13 deficiency, ultralarge von Willebrand multimers) from hemolytic uremic syndrome (Shiga toxin of E. coli O157:H7 injuring renal endothelium), noting schistocytes, thrombocytopenia, and normal PT and PTT in both.
HE-9-B.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Infectious and immunologic: thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, hemolytic uremic syndrome

HE-9-B.t: Explain how prosthetic heart valves and severe aortic stenosis cause mechanical intravascular hemolysis with schistocytes, and predict the iron deficiency that can follow chronic hemoglobinuria.
HE-9-B.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Traumatic, mechanical, and vascular disorders: mechanical erythrocyte injury

HE-9-B.t: Identify causes of splenic rupture (blunt trauma, mononucleosis splenomegaly), infarct (sickle cell disease, emboli), and abscess (septic emboli from endocarditis), and predict post-splenectomy smear findings (Howell-Jolly bodies, target cells, thrombocytosis).
HE-9-B.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Traumatic, mechanical, and vascular disorders: splenic rupture, infarct, abscess, splenectomy effects

HE-9-B.t: Explain how hypersplenism from portal hypertension or infiltrative disease causes cytopenias by splenic sequestration, and distinguish it from marrow failure by marrow cellularity and splenomegaly.
HE-9-B.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Traumatic, mechanical, and vascular disorders: hypersplenism

HE-9-C.t: Identify triggers of DIC (sepsis, trauma, placental abruption, amniotic fluid embolism, acute promyelocytic leukemia, mucin-secreting adenocarcinoma) and predict thrombocytopenia, prolonged PT and PTT, low fibrinogen, high D-dimer, and schistocytes.
HE-9-C.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Coagulation disorders: disseminated intravascular coagulation

HE-9-C.t: Relate microthrombi in DIC to ischemic injury of kidney, lung, brain, and adrenal glands, and consumption of platelets and clotting factors to simultaneous bleeding from venipuncture sites and mucosa.
HE-9-C.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Coagulation disorders: disseminated intravascular coagulation

HE-9-C.t: Distinguish hemophilia A (factor VIII) from hemophilia B (factor IX) as X-linked deficiencies with hemarthroses and deep muscle bleeds, isolated prolonged PTT, and correction on mixing, unlike an acquired factor VIII inhibitor.
HE-9-C.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Coagulation disorders: hemophilia A, hemophilia B

HE-9-C.t: Explain how IgG autoantibodies against platelet GpIIb/IIIa cause splenic platelet destruction in ITP, and contrast acute childhood ITP after viral infection with chronic adult ITP, both showing isolated thrombocytopenia and increased marrow megakaryocytes.
HE-9-C.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Anemia, cytopenias, and polycythemia: immune thrombocytopenic purpura

HE-9-C.t: Explain how von Willebrand factor deficiency impairs platelet adhesion and factor VIII stability, and predict mucosal bleeding, prolonged bleeding time, normal platelet count, normal or prolonged PTT, and decreased ristocetin cofactor activity.
HE-9-C.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Coagulation disorders: von Willebrand disease

HE-9-C.t: Identify causes of vitamin K deficiency (newborns not given prophylaxis, fat malabsorption, prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotics, poor intake) and explain why the PT prolongs first, since factor VII has the shortest half-life.
HE-9-C.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Nutrition: vitamin deficiencies and/or toxicities: vitamin K

HE-9-C.t: Contrast the coagulation profile of liver failure (prolonged PT and PTT, low fibrinogen, thrombocytopenia, normal or high factor VIII) with that of vitamin K deficiency (prolonged PT, normal fibrinogen and platelets).
HE-9-C.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Coagulation disorders: hypofibrinogenemia

HE-9-C.t: Distinguish Bernard-Soulier syndrome (GpIb deficiency, large platelets, defective adhesion), Glanzmann thrombasthenia (GpIIb/IIIa deficiency, defective aggregation), and uremic platelet dysfunction by mechanism and platelet findings.
HE-9-C.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Coagulation disorders: qualitative platelet dysfunction

HE-9-C.t: Explain how inherited antithrombin III, protein C, or protein S deficiency and hyperhomocysteinemia increase venous thrombosis risk, and identify features that suggest an inherited thrombophilia (young age, recurrent or unusual-site clots, family history).
HE-9-C.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Coagulation disorders: hypercoagulable: antithrombin III, protein C, protein S deficiency, homocysteinemia

HE-9-C.t: Identify hematologic paraneoplastic syndromes: migratory thrombophlebitis (Trousseau syndrome) with pancreatic and other adenocarcinomas, erythrocytosis from ectopic erythropoietin (renal cell and hepatocellular carcinoma), and pure red cell aplasia with thymoma.
HE-9-C.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Neoplasms: paraneoplastic syndromes: hematologic

HE-9-D.t: Describe acute lymphoblastic leukemia as a TdT-positive lymphoblast neoplasm, mainly of children, presenting with marrow failure and bone pain, with CNS and testicular spread and increased risk in Down syndrome.
HE-9-D.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Neoplasms: acute lymphoblastic leukemia

HE-9-D.t: Describe acute myeloid leukemia (usually at least 20% marrow blasts, myeloperoxidase-positive Auer rods, mainly adults), its risk factors (prior chemotherapy, radiation, benzene, myelodysplasia, Down syndrome), and the link between acute promyelocytic leukemia and DIC.
HE-9-D.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Neoplasms: acute myeloid leukemia

HE-9-D.t: Describe chronic lymphocytic leukemia as a CD5-positive, CD23-positive mature B cell neoplasm of older adults with smudge cells, hypogammaglobulinemia, warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia, and Richter transformation to diffuse large B cell lymphoma.
HE-9-D.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Neoplasms: chronic lymphocytic leukemia

HE-9-D.t: Describe chronic myeloid leukemia (neutrophilia across all maturation stages, basophilia, splenomegaly), its confirmation by detecting t(9;22) BCR-ABL1, and progression from chronic phase to accelerated phase and blast crisis.
HE-9-D.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Neoplasms: chronic myeloid leukemia

HE-9-D.t: Identify hairy cell leukemia by mature B cells with hairlike projections, TRAP and CD11c positivity, BRAF V600E mutation, a dry tap from marrow fibrosis, and massive splenomegaly without lymphadenopathy.

Distinguish Hodgkin lymphoma (CD15 and CD30 positive Reed-Sternberg cells, contiguous nodal spread, bimodal age, EBV association, nodular sclerosis most common) from non-Hodgkin lymphoma (noncontiguous spread, frequent extranodal involvement).
HE-9-D.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Neoplasms: Hodgkin lymphoma

HE-9-D.t: Relate major non-Hodgkin lymphomas to their features: diffuse large B cell (most common, aggressive), follicular (t(14;18), indolent), Burkitt (t(8;14), starry sky, EBV), mantle cell (t(11;14), CD5 positive), and MALT lymphoma (Helicobacter pylori).
HE-9-D.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Neoplasms: non-Hodgkin lymphoma, Burkitt lymphoma

HE-9-D.t: Describe T cell lymphomas: adult T cell leukemia/lymphoma (HTLV-1, hypercalcemia, lytic bone lesions) and mycosis fungoides (skin-homing CD4 T cells, Pautrier microabscesses, Sezary cells in blood).
HE-9-D.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Neoplasms: T-cell lymphoma

HE-9-D.t: Explain how clonal plasma cells in multiple myeloma cause hypercalcemia and punched-out lytic lesions (osteoclast activation through RANKL), renal injury from light chain casts, anemia, rouleaux, infections, and an M spike on electrophoresis.
HE-9-D.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Neoplasms: multiple myeloma

HE-9-D.t: Distinguish multiple myeloma from MGUS (M protein below 3 g/dL, under 10% marrow plasma cells, no end-organ damage) and from Waldenström macroglobulinemia (IgM, hyperviscosity, no lytic lesions), and relate light chains to AL amyloidosis.
HE-9-D.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Neoplasms: MGUS, Waldenström macroglobulinemia, dysproteinemias

HE-9-D.t: Describe myelodysplastic syndromes as clonal, ineffective hematopoiesis in older adults or after alkylating agents or radiation, with cytopenias, dysplastic cells (pseudo-Pelger-Huet neutrophils, ringed sideroblasts), and risk of progression to AML.
HE-9-D.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Neoplasms: myelodysplastic syndrome

HE-9-D.t: Describe primary myelofibrosis (JAK2, CALR, or MPL mutation, megakaryocyte-driven marrow fibrosis, dry tap, teardrop cells, leukoerythroblastic smear) and massive splenomegaly from extramedullary hematopoiesis.

Describe Langerhans cell histiocytosis as a clonal proliferation of CD1a-positive, S100-positive Langerhans cells with Birbeck granules, presenting in children with lytic bone lesions (eosinophilic granuloma) or multisystem disease with diabetes insipidus.
HE-9-D.usmle: Multisystem Processes & Disorders: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: Langerhans cell histiocytosis

HE-9-D.t: Explain how rapid lysis of high-turnover tumors (Burkitt lymphoma, acute leukemias) during treatment causes tumor lysis syndrome, and predict hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia, hyperuricemia, and acute kidney injury.
HE-9-D.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Adverse effects of drugs: tumor lysis syndrome

HE-9-E.t: Identify risk factors for severe babesiosis (asplenia, older age, immunosuppression) and predict fever, hemolytic anemia, and thrombocytopenia after a tick bite in the northeastern or upper midwestern United States.
HE-9-E.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Infectious and immunologic: babesiosis

HE-9-E.t: Relate the cyclic fevers of malaria to synchronized rupture of infected red cells (about 48 hours for P. vivax and P. ovale, 72 hours for P. malariae) and predict hemolytic anemia, splenomegaly, and thrombocytopenia.
HE-9-E.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Infectious and immunologic: malaria

HE-9-E.t: Predict complications of Plasmodium falciparum malaria (cerebral malaria, severe anemia, hypoglycemia, acute kidney injury, hemoglobinuria, acute respiratory distress) and identify multiple ring forms and banana-shaped gametocytes on a thin smear.
HE-9-E.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Infectious and immunologic: malaria

HE-9-E.t: Explain how granulomatous reactions to trapped Schistosoma eggs cause presinusoidal portal hypertension with periportal pipestem fibrosis (S. mansoni) and hematuria, bladder fibrosis, and squamous cell carcinoma (S. haematobium), with eosinophilia.

Compare dengue, chikungunya, and Zika as Aedes-transmitted viruses: severe dengue with thrombocytopenia and plasma leakage after reinfection with another serotype, persistent arthralgia in chikungunya, and congenital microcephaly with Zika.
HE-9-E.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Infectious and immunologic: viral: dengue, chikungunya, Zika

HE-9-E.t: Describe Ebola and Marburg filoviruses: spread by contact with infected body fluids, fruit bats as the likely reservoir, and fever with vomiting, diarrhea, hemorrhage, DIC, and multiorgan failure.
HE-9-E.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Infectious and immunologic: viral hemorrhagic fever

HE-9-E.t: Describe Yersinia pestis (rodent flea vector, bipolar staining, painful suppurative bubo, septicemic and pneumonic spread) and Bartonella henselae (cat scratch, regional lymphadenopathy with stellate necrotizing granulomas) as causes of lymphadenitis.
HE-9-E.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Infectious and immunologic: bubonic plague, cat-scratch disease

HE-9-E.t: Describe acute lymphangitis from Streptococcus pyogenes (red streaks tracking toward regional nodes) and distinguish reactive lymphadenitis patterns (follicular hyperplasia, paracortical hyperplasia, sinus histiocytosis) from lymphoma.
HE-9-E.usmle: Blood & Lymphoreticular System: Infectious and immunologic: lymphangitis, lymphadenitis
